1.explanation: In current Carbon React (v10.x), the <Select> component only supports an “invalid” state via the `invalid` and `invalidText` props. There is no built-in `warn` or `warnText` API yet. This snippet attempts to pass `warn` & `warnText` exactly like `invalid` & `invalidText`. As a result, nothing changes visually. That reproduces the bug: you can see there is no warning icon, no yellow border, and no helper text, despite passing these props. Once the warning state API is implemented, this same code should render the yellow‐styled Select shown in the mockups.
1.bug_scenario: We’re trying to add a “warning” (yellow) state to the Carbon <Select> component, similar to the existing error (red) state. In the mockups you can see that when you pass a `warn` prop and a `warnText` to the Select it should: 1) render the warning-filled icon (16px, support-03 fill, black inner fill) to the right of the label area, 2) apply a yellow border (support-07) on focus or blur, and 3) render the warning message below the control in the same style as the invalidText. Currently, if you try to pass `warn` / `warnText` to the component, nothing happens – no icon, no border color, no message.
